title: C1551B — Powertrain control module (PCM) connector
introduction:
I read this connector reference as a switchboard directory: some connections carry commands, others carry reports, reference supplies or returns. The fuel-pump command and monitor entries make the distinction especially useful—asking for something to happen and hearing back about it are different conversations.

Use the connector identification to confirm the reference, locate a printed cavity label in the drawing, then read across its assignment row. The table connects that position with a circuit identifier and its recorded function. Shaded and outlined positions help your eye follow the drawing, but there is no supplied shading legend; the table remains the basis for interpreting an assignment.

This is a connector and circuit lookup guide. Physical viewing direction, access and disconnection, test conditions and replacement-wire selection require separate service information. The gauge convention and the Size and Used codes are not explained here, and blank qualifiers do not establish vehicle applicability. The metadata and drawing also differ on cavity count; leave that discrepancy unresolved rather than inventing a missing position.

The repeated post-catalyst oxygen-sensor circuit row has alternative wire colors without a qualifier selecting between them. Keep both records; this reference does not establish which color applies to a particular vehicle.

edits.why: As displayed, the broad cavity bank sits to the right of a narrow side bank. Within each bank, the printed labels decrease from left to right and increase down the page. I use those labels and the housing outline to stay oriented on the drawing. This describes the page layout only; it does not identify a wire-side or mating-side view. The outer housing projections have no established release or locking function in this evidence.

Find the matching Cavity row, then read Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function, Qualifier, Used and Terminal Part Number together. Function distinguishes such roles as fan control, pedal-related connections, reference supplies, returns, fuel-pump command and fuel-pump monitoring. A control or relay label identifies the recorded association; it does not establish a direct motor-power feed or a separately replaceable relay. Keep blank entries and unexplained codes literal. Once the relevant circuit is identified, use its applicable diagnostic instructions for setup, measurements and the next decision; this directory alone cannot establish whether a component or the controller has failed.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata states Pin Count 104, while the supplied illustration shows cavity labels 1–103. The evidence does not reconcile the difference; review is needed before presenting the illustration as a complete view matching that count.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 124 primary units, six complete pages/one figure and two edits. Original first CLI author covered 55 units/two headings. Original count disagreement retained; introduction additionally discloses unqualified post-catalyst sensor wire-color alternatives. Other public fields remain equal to original author. Original partial author remains separate; physical count and unqualified gauge/terminal alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
